stem:
Asha writes △ABC ≅ △DEF. She needs the side that corresponds to side AB.

Which statement is correct?

options.text: Any side that looks the same length as AB corresponds, whatever the vertex order.
Correspondence still holds even when the vertex order does not make equal sides overlap.
A non-corresponding angle that looks equal to angle A settles which side matches AB.
Side DE corresponds to AB, because A matches D and B matches E in the congruence statement.

teacher.key_rationale: In △ABC ≅ △DEF, vertices match in written order, so AB corresponds to DE. Treating any equal-looking length as corresponding substitutes a weaker label for vertex order. Dropping the overlap requirement omits the defining condition. Using a non-corresponding equal-looking angle is outside this correspondence hinge.

mx_swap.reason: Printed-letter capture is weaker here than equal-looking-side substitution, missing-overlap omission, and non-corresponding-angle scope error; kept those three.
